blocks.raw: # Customer entity
blocks.text: Customer entity

blocks.raw: This page provides you with information on customer entity
blocks.text: This page provides you with information on customer entity

blocks.raw: The Customer entity is the focal point around which all our data revolves. This entity includes information about each customer, ranging from essential contact details to demographic and geographic data. In addition, It also includes information about their purchase history, behavioural activities, loyalty details, the user groups they are part of, reward and coupon details and other related information.

blocks.raw: Within this framework, the source through which a customer is registered is called a customer data source. This source serves as the initial touchpoint, capturing the basic details that contribute to the making of a customer profile. Additionally, the channels available for communication with the customer are referred to as customer communication channels. These channels play a pivotal role in establishing meaningful connections and fostering effective communication with customers.

blocks.raw: # Understanding data sources
blocks.text: Understanding data sources

blocks.raw: In our system, a "Source" refers to the origin or system from which customer information is integrated. Each source represents a unique system, integration, or data feed.

blocks.raw: Customers may be represented differently across various sources. For instance, a customer named "Christopher" in one source could appear as "Christo" in another. This discrepancy underscores the necessity for identity resolution to establish a unified and accurate view of the customer.

blocks.raw: Data integration involves collecting information from different sources, including identifiers, subscription statuses, and email addresses. This process merges and creates a consolidated, reliable customer profile. When the system receives information from the same identifier already present but from a different source, it analyzes, [merges](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/manage-change-request#merge-accounts), and adds it to the existing customer profile under a different source.

blocks.raw: # Understanding communication channels
blocks.text: Understanding communication channels

blocks.raw:
A "Communication Channel" represents the medium through which customers receive messages. Examples include SMS, push notifications, web engagement, and POS (Point of Sale) systems.\
Some sources may act as both a source and a communication channel. For instance, WeChat not only provides customer information but also serves as a communication channel. Communication channels can vary, and information may be collected from diverse sources. For instance, a customer's communication channel, such as WeChat, may exclusively come from the WeChat system. Overlapping scenarios may arise where the source and communication channel are the same, while in other cases, they can be different. The system is designed to handle these variations effectively.

blocks.raw:
<Callout icon="🚧" theme="warn">
  **Deleted status and PII deletion**

  If `CONF_ENABLE_PII_DELETION` is enabled for your organization, you cannot change a customer's status to Deleted using the standard status update API or the Membercare status-change UI. Attempting to do so returns error code `UPDATECUSTOMERSTATUS_1032` with the message: "Customer update with pending deletion or deleted status not allowed."

  When PII deletion is enabled, the Deleted status is a reserved system state. The platform sets it automatically only after a PII deletion request is raised and approved through the proper flow.

  To move a customer to Deleted status, use the PII deletion flow:

  1. In Membercare, open the customer's profile and click the three-dots menu.
  2. From the ID change request dropdown, select **Delete member's account** and submit the request.
  3. A user with approver access must approve the request.

  Once approved, the customer's status moves to Pending Deletion, and then to Deleted after the configured waiting period lapses.

  For full details, see [Performing Data Deletion](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/performing-data-deletion).
</Callout>

blocks.raw: # Managing loyalty status
blocks.text: Managing loyalty status

blocks.raw: A customer can be of two types: a loyalty customer and a non-loyalty customer. A loyalty customer is a registered member of your organization's loyalty program, while non-loyalty customers are those who have not enrolled in your loyalty program but have subscribed using their mobile number or email ID with the organization. Transactions for these customers are tagged to their respective identifiers (mobile number/email ID).

Transactions for these customers are tagged to their respective identifiers (mobile number/email ID).

blocks.raw: # Managing test and control status
blocks.text: Managing test and control status

blocks.raw: The customer list is split into a test and control group. Customers in the test audience group receive campaign communications, while those in the control audience group do not. The test and control statuses are displayed based on the group to which they belong. These statuses are maintained by the brands or auto-assigned and can be changed either through  [Member Care](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/customer_overview#customer-status-and-name) or [Connect+](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/test_and_control).

blocks.raw: # External ID configuration
blocks.text: External ID configuration

blocks.raw: You can use the below configurations to enable the generation of a customised external ID for customers. Once this configuration is enabled, the external ID in the customer add API payload will be replaced with the generated external ID.
blocks.text: You can use the below configurations to enable the generation of a customised external ID for customers. Once this configuration is enabled, the external ID in the customer add API payload will be replaced with the generated external ID.

blocks.raw:
> **Important**
>
> The system strictly enforces both the prefix and length for External IDs during customer import and API operations. These requirements are set in Org Settings > Registration. Only External IDs that match the configured prefix (for example, LM\*) and the exact length (for example, 10 digits) are accepted. If an External ID does not meet these requirements, the system rejects the record during both import and API workflows. Rejected records are not processed, which can impact event processing and eligibility updates for those customers. Ensure that all External IDs, whether imported or submitted via API, meet the required prefix and length to avoid data loss or processing failures.
blocks.text: ImportantThe system strictly enforces both the prefix and length for External IDs during customer import and API operations. These requirements are set in Org Settings > Registration. Only External IDs that match the configured prefix (for example, LM*) and the exact length (for example, 10 digits) are accepted. If an External ID does not meet these requirements, the system rejects the record during both import and API workflows. Rejected records are not processed, which can impact event processing and eligibility updates for those customers. Ensure that all External IDs, whether imported or submitted via API, meet the required prefix and length to avoid data loss or processing failures.

blocks.raw:
> **Failure scenarios**
>
> External ID generation may fail in the following cases:
>
> * If all possible candidate external IDs within the allowed retry limit are already assigned to existing customers, the system cannot generate a new unique external ID. In this case, the registration fails and the customer profile is not created.
> * If the highest external ID in the database does not match the configured prefix or suffix, the system may not be able to increment the counter correctly. This can cause the external ID generation process to skip updating the internal counter, resulting in missing external IDs for new registrations.
>
> These failures can prevent new customer registrations and may cause downstream integration issues. To avoid these problems, regularly review your external ID configuration, including prefix, suffix, and length, and ensure that the available ID range is sufficient for your expected registration volume.

Configuration & Description Value

CONF_CARD_CHECKSUM_DIGIT_ALGO (Mandatory) Defines the algorithm to generate the checksum. The checksum is added as the last digit of the external ID. LUHN_ALGO (MOD10), MOD7_ALGO, AUTO_INC, RANDOM, RANDOM_LUHN, RANDOM_MOD7
CONF_CARD_NUMBER_LENGTH (Mandatory) Defines the external ID length. This is the total length of the external id including prefix, suffix, and checksum. Example: If card number length = 12, Prefix = 1234, Suffix = 3401, Offset = 3000, and algorithm = AUTO_INC, then card number can be 123430003401. **Note:** Suffix is not applicable for MOD7 and LUHN_ALGO (MOD10) algorithms. Integers ranging from 1-50.
CONF_CARD_NUMBER_OFFSET (Optional) Defines the offset value for the external ID. For example for a card number series with offset value 3000, can be 111200000030004, 111200000030015 etc. Any integer value
CONF_CARD_NUMBER_PREFIX (Optional) Defines the prefix for the external ID number. Any integer value but prefix + suffix + system-generated number should not be more than 50.
CONF_CARD_NUMBER_SUFFIX (Optional) Defines the SUFFIX for the external ID number. This is only applicable for AUTO_INC alogrithm. Any integer value but prefix + suffix + system-generated number should not be more than 50.
CONF_VALUES_TO_INCLUDE_FOR_CHECKSUM_DIGIT (Optional) Specifies whether the prefix should be considered when generating the checksum value. PREFIX - Prefix is considered NONE - Prefix is not considered

blocks.raw: # Dual eligibility
blocks.text: Dual eligibility

blocks.raw: The Dual Eligibility feature allows you to register multiple users with the same secondary identifiers. When the Dual Eligibility feature is enabled, only one identifier is considered the primary identifier and the rest of the identifiers are considered for communication. The primary identifier for both of these profiles must be unique.
blocks.text: The Dual Eligibility feature allows you to register multiple users with the same secondary identifiers. When the Dual Eligibility feature is enabled, only one identifier is considered the primary identifier and the rest of the identifiers are considered for communication. The primary identifier for both of these profiles must be unique.

blocks.raw: **Example:** Consider a brand user who is registered on the platform using Email <abc@example.com>, Mobile 123-456-7890 (primary identifier), and External ID ABC123. With the Dual Eligibility feature enabled, another user can be registered again using Email <abc@example.com> and External ID ABC124.
blocks.text: Example: Consider a brand user who is registered on the platform using Email abc@example.com, Mobile 123-456-7890 (primary identifier), and External ID ABC123. With the Dual Eligibility feature enabled, another user can be registered again using Email abc@example.com and External ID ABC124.

blocks.raw: **Notes:**
blocks.text: Notes:

blocks.raw: * For the users registered with Dual Eligibility, the information about the user can be retrieved only using the primary identifier.
blocks.text: For the users registered with Dual Eligibility, the information about the user can be retrieved only using the primary identifier.
